source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public Job 41:1–8 binds Hebrew 40:25–32; public 41:9–34 binds Hebrew 41:1–26. Other selected labels match. All 458 original records bind once in this batch; earlier chapters 1–26 are unchanged.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains renewed discourse without assigning a different speaker.
verses.before: Job again took up his discourse and said:
verses.after: Job continued his discourse:
verses.tsw_comparator: Job again took up his discourse and said:

verses.rationale: Keeps the oath addressed through accusation, not softened piety.
verses.before: “As God lives, who has taken away my justice, and the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter,
verses.after: “As God lives, who has denied me justice, and the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter,
verses.tsw_comparator: “As God lives, who has taken away my justice, and the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter,

verses.rationale: Preserves paired breath images grounding the oath in life.
verses.before: as long as my breath is in me and the spirit of God is in my nostrils,
verses.after: as long as breath remains in me and God’s breath is in my nostrils,
verses.tsw_comparator: as long as my breath is in me and the spirit of God is in my nostrils,

verses.rationale: Makes the oath’s negative force natural and direct.
verses.before: my lips will surely not speak injustice, and my tongue will not utter deceit.
verses.after: my lips will speak no injustice, and my tongue will utter no deceit.
verses.tsw_comparator: my lips will surely not speak injustice, and my tongue will not utter deceit.

verses.rationale: Connects refusal to vindicate the friends with integrity.
verses.before: Far be it from me to declare you righteous! Until I expire, I will not put away my integrity from me.
verses.after: I will never admit that you are right! Until I die, I will not let go of my integrity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Far be it from me to declare you righteous! Until I expire, I will not put away my integrity from me.

verses.rationale: Keeps conscience and lifetime claim within Job’s speech.
verses.before: I hold fast my righteousness and will not let it go; my heart does not reproach me for any of my days.
verses.after: I hold firmly to my righteousness and will not release it; my heart reproaches me for none of my days.
verses.tsw_comparator: I hold fast my righteousness and will not let it go; my heart does not reproach me for any of my days.

verses.rationale: Preserves the wish against opponents, not a generic prediction.
verses.before: Let my enemy be like the wicked, and the one who rises against me like the unjust.
verses.after: Let my enemy fare like the wicked, and anyone who rises against me like the unjust.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let my enemy be like the wicked, and the one who rises against me like the unjust.

verses.rationale: Selects cutting-off sense; gain alternative belongs in note.
verses.before: For what is the hope of the godless when God cuts him off, when God takes away his life?
verses.after: What hope has the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
verses.tsw_comparator: For what is the hope of the godless when God cuts him off, when God takes away his life?

verses.rationale: Keeps rhetorical question and impending distress.
verses.before: Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?
verses.after: Will God hear his cry when trouble comes upon him?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?

verses.rationale: Preserves delight alongside sustained appeal.
verses.before: Will he delight himself in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?
verses.after: Will he delight in the Almighty and call on God at all times?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will he delight himself in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?

verses.rationale: Retains hand image and Job’s claimed knowledge.
verses.before: I will teach you about the hand of God; what is with the Almighty I will not conceal.
verses.after: I will teach you about God’s hand; I will not conceal what is with the Almighty.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will teach you about the hand of God; what is with the Almighty I will not conceal.

verses.rationale: Makes emphatic empty speech intelligible without removing rebuke.
verses.before: Look, all of you have seen it. Why then do you become completely empty?
verses.after: You have all seen this yourselves. Why, then, do you keep talking such emptiness?
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, all of you have seen it. Why then do you become completely empty?

verses.rationale: Keeps received speaker and inheritance formula despite tension.
verses.before: This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the inheritance ruthless people receive from the Almighty:
verses.after: This is the wicked person’s portion from God, the inheritance the ruthless receive from the Almighty:
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the inheritance ruthless people receive from the Almighty:

verses.rationale: Preserves children’s violent fate and hunger as Job’s claim.
verses.before: If his children multiply, it is for the sword, and his offspring will not be satisfied with bread.
verses.after: however many his children, they are destined for the sword; his descendants will not have enough bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: If his children multiply, it is for the sword, and his offspring will not be satisfied with bread.

verses.rationale: Follows read plural survivors; retains personified death.
verses.before: People who survive him will be buried by death, and his widows will not weep.
verses.after: Those who survive him will be buried by death, and his widows will not weep.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who survive him will be buried by death, and his widows will not weep.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired accumulated wealth and earth imagery.
verses.before: Though he heaps up silver like dust and prepares clothing like clay,
verses.after: Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up clothing like clay,
verses.tsw_comparator: Though he heaps up silver like dust and prepares clothing like clay,

verses.rationale: Connects repeated piling with reversal of ownership.
verses.before: he may prepare it, but the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide the silver.
verses.after: he may pile it up, but the righteous will wear it; the innocent will divide the silver.
verses.tsw_comparator: he may prepare it, but the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide the silver.

verses.rationale: Retains fragile moth house rather than substituting nest.
verses.before: He builds his house like a moth, like a shelter a watchman makes.
verses.after: He builds his house like a moth’s, like a shelter a watchman makes.
verses.tsw_comparator: He builds his house like a moth, like a shelter a watchman makes.

verses.rationale: Retains difficult gathered wording with alternative in note.
verses.before: He lies down rich, but he will not do so again; he opens his eyes, and it is gone.
verses.after: He lies down wealthy, but will not be gathered; he opens his eyes, and it is gone.
verses.tsw_comparator: He lies down rich, but he will not do so again; he opens his eyes, and it is gone.

verses.rationale: Unfolds water and night-storm images naturally.
verses.before: Terrors overtake him like waters; at night a whirlwind steals him away.
verses.after: Terrors overtake him like a flood; a storm carries him off in the night.
verses.tsw_comparator: Terrors overtake him like waters; at night a whirlwind steals him away.

verses.rationale: Keeps east wind and forcible displacement.
verses.before: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him from his place.
verses.after: The east wind lifts him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him from his place.

verses.rationale: Continues wind as subject; divine subject remains possible.
verses.before: It hurls itself against him and does not spare; he desperately flees from its hand.
verses.after: It hurls itself at him without pity; he struggles to flee its grasp.
verses.tsw_comparator: It hurls itself against him and does not spare; he desperately flees from its hand.

verses.rationale: Retains personification and dismissive hissing image.
verses.before: It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place.”
verses.after: It claps its hands at him and whistles him out of his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place.”

verses.rationale: Opens mining poem without adding a speaker change.
verses.before: “Surely there is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined.
verses.after: There is a place where silver is mined, and a place where gold is refined.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Surely there is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined.

verses.rationale: Preserves distinct metals and extraction processes.
verses.before: Iron is taken from the dust, and copper is smelted from stone.
verses.after: Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from stone.
verses.tsw_comparator: Iron is taken from the dust, and copper is smelted from stone.

verses.rationale: Names human agents implicit in mining sequence.
verses.before: A human puts an end to darkness and searches to the farthest limit for stone in gloom and death-shadow.
verses.after: People put an end to darkness; they search to the farthest depths for stone in gloom and deep shadow.
verses.tsw_comparator: A human puts an end to darkness and searches to the farthest limit for stone in gloom and death-shadow.

verses.rationale: Renders difficult mining scene with hanging workers intact.
verses.before: He opens a shaft far from where people dwell, forgotten by the foot; they hang and swing far from humanity.
verses.after: They cut a shaft far from inhabited places; forgotten by passing feet, they hang and sway far from other people.
verses.tsw_comparator: He opens a shaft far from where people dwell, forgotten by the foot; they hang and swing far from humanity.

verses.rationale: Keeps contrast of surface nourishment and underground disruption.
verses.before: As for the earth, from it comes bread, but underneath it is overturned as by fire.
verses.after: The earth brings forth bread, but beneath it things are overturned as by fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the earth, from it comes bread, but underneath it is overturned as by fire.

verses.rationale: Uses conventional ancient blue-stone identification with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: Its stones are the place of sapphire, and its dust contains gold.
verses.after: Its stones hold lapis lazuli, and its dust contains gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its stones are the place of sapphire, and its dust contains gold.

verses.rationale: Preserves exceptional human access beyond sharp avian sight.
verses.before: A path no bird of prey knows, and the falcon’s eye has not seen it.
verses.after: No bird of prey knows that path; the falcon’s eye has never seen it.
verses.tsw_comparator: A path no bird of prey knows, and the falcon’s eye has not seen it.

verses.rationale: Retains paired beast images rather than explaining away.
verses.before: Proud beasts have not trodden it; the lion has not passed over it.
verses.after: Proud beasts have not trodden it; no lion has passed over it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Proud beasts have not trodden it; the lion has not passed over it.

verses.rationale: Makes miner’s agency audible while retaining vast image.
verses.before: A human puts his hand to the flint; he overturns mountains by the roots.
verses.after: People lay hands on flint and overturn mountains at their roots.
verses.tsw_comparator: A human puts his hand to the flint; he overturns mountains by the roots.

verses.rationale: Retains cutting and seeing as linked mining actions.
verses.before: He cuts channels through the rocks, and his eye sees every precious thing.
verses.after: They cut channels through the rocks; their eyes discover every precious thing.
verses.tsw_comparator: He cuts channels through the rocks, and his eye sees every precious thing.

verses.rationale: Selects source/seepage sense of difficult weeping-stream phrase.
verses.before: He binds the streams from weeping, and brings hidden things to light.
verses.after: They stop up streams at their sources and bring hidden things into the light.
verses.tsw_comparator: He binds the streams from weeping, and brings hidden things to light.

verses.rationale: Introduces recurring question with accessible home image.
verses.before: But wisdom—where can it be found? And where is the place of understanding?
verses.after: But where can wisdom be found? Where is the home of understanding?
verses.tsw_comparator: But wisdom—where can it be found? And where is the place of understanding?

verses.rationale: Follows pinned worth, not substituted way.
verses.before: A human does not know its value, and it is not found in the land of the living.
verses.after: No mortal knows its worth; it cannot be found in the land of the living.
verses.tsw_comparator: A human does not know its value, and it is not found in the land of the living.

verses.rationale: Preserves personified separate denials.
verses.before: The deep says, ‘It is not in me,’ and the sea says, ‘It is not with me.’
verses.after: The deep says, ‘It is not in me.’ The sea says, ‘It is not with me.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The deep says, ‘It is not in me,’ and the sea says, ‘It is not with me.’

verses.rationale: Keeps payment and weighing rather than abstract pricelessness.
verses.before: Fine gold cannot be given for it, and silver cannot be weighed as its price.
verses.after: Fine gold cannot be given in exchange for it, nor silver weighed out as its price.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fine gold cannot be given for it, and silver cannot be weighed as its price.

verses.rationale: Retains place and distinct stones with qualified identification.
verses.before: It cannot be weighed against gold of Ophir, against precious onyx or sapphire.
verses.after: It cannot be valued in gold from Ophir, in precious onyx or lapis lazuli.
verses.tsw_comparator: It cannot be weighed against gold of Ophir, against precious onyx or sapphire.

verses.rationale: Preserves glass as ancient valuable material.
verses.before: Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor can it be exchanged for a vessel of refined gold.
verses.after: Gold and glass cannot equal it; it cannot be exchanged for vessels of pure gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor can it be exchanged for a vessel of refined gold.

verses.rationale: Uses conventional uncertain material names, not modern certainty.
verses.before: Coral and crystal need not be mentioned; the acquisition of wisdom is above pearls.
verses.after: Coral and crystal are not worth mentioning; the price of wisdom is beyond pearls.
verses.tsw_comparator: Coral and crystal need not be mentioned; the acquisition of wisdom is above pearls.

verses.rationale: Retains Cush and comparison’s repeated valuation language.
verses.before: The topaz of Cush cannot equal it; it cannot be weighed against pure gold.
verses.after: Topaz from Cush cannot equal it; it cannot be valued in pure gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: The topaz of Cush cannot equal it; it cannot be weighed against pure gold.

verses.rationale: Repeats question while preserving find/come distinction.
verses.before: From where then does wisdom come? And where is the place of understanding?
verses.after: Where, then, does wisdom come from? Where is the home of understanding?
verses.tsw_comparator: From where then does wisdom come? And where is the place of understanding?

verses.rationale: Keeps universal hiddenness and avian parallel.
verses.before: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing and concealed from the birds of the heavens.
verses.after: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing, concealed even from the birds of the heavens.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing and concealed from the birds of the heavens.

verses.rationale: Retains personified death realm and indirect knowledge.
verses.before: Abaddon and Death say, ‘With our ears we have heard a report of it.’
verses.after: Abaddon and Death say, ‘We have heard only a report of it.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Abaddon and Death say, ‘With our ears we have heard a report of it.’

verses.rationale: Contrasts divine knowledge with human searching.
verses.before: God understands the way to it, and he knows its place.
verses.after: God understands the way to it; he knows where it lives.
verses.tsw_comparator: God understands the way to it, and he knows its place.

verses.rationale: Preserves comprehensive sight across both lines.
verses.before: For he looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.
verses.after: For he looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything beneath the heavens.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.

verses.rationale: Keeps physical creation images without scientific expansion.
verses.before: When he gave weight to the wind and measured the waters by measure,
verses.after: When he gave weight to the wind and measured out the waters,
verses.tsw_comparator: When he gave weight to the wind and measured the waters by measure,

verses.rationale: Retains rain’s ordinance and storm’s path.
verses.before: when he made a decree for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
verses.after: when he set a rule for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
verses.tsw_comparator: when he made a decree for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,

verses.rationale: Preserves four distinct divine actions concerning wisdom.
verses.before: then he saw wisdom and declared it; he established it and also searched it out.
verses.after: then he saw wisdom and declared it; he established it and searched it out.
verses.tsw_comparator: then he saw wisdom and declared it; he established it and also searched it out.

verses.rationale: Uses Lord for Adonai; retains wisdom’s paired conclusion.
verses.before: And he said to humanity: ‘Look, the fear of the Lord—that is wisdom, and turning away from evil is understanding.’”
verses.after: And he said to humanity, ‘Look: reverence for the Lord is wisdom, and turning from evil is understanding.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to humanity: ‘Look, the fear of the Lord—that is wisdom, and turning away from evil is understanding.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps explicit resumed discourse boundary.
verses.before: Job again took up his discourse and said:
verses.after: Job continued his discourse:
verses.tsw_comparator: Job again took up his discourse and said:

verses.rationale: Makes longing for remembered protection audible.
verses.before: “If only I were as in former months, as in the days when God watched over me,
verses.after: “If only I could return to the months gone by, to the days when God watched over me,
verses.tsw_comparator: “If only I were as in former months, as in the days when God watched over me,

verses.rationale: Retains lamp and walking images.
verses.before: when his lamp shone upon my head and by his light I walked through darkness,
verses.after: when his lamp shone above my head and by his light I walked through darkness!
verses.tsw_comparator: when his lamp shone upon my head and by his light I walked through darkness,

verses.rationale: Selects prime and intimate counsel senses with note.
verses.before: as I was in the days of my prime, when the counsel of God was over my tent,
verses.after: If only I were as in my prime, when God’s friendship rested over my tent,
verses.tsw_comparator: as I was in the days of my prime, when the counsel of God was over my tent,

verses.rationale: Reads youths as children in remembered household.
verses.before: when the Almighty was still with me, when my children were around me,
verses.after: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were all around me,
verses.tsw_comparator: when the Almighty was still with me, when my children were around me,

verses.rationale: Preserves extravagant abundance without domesticating imagery.
verses.before: when my steps were washed with curds and the rock poured out streams of oil for me.
verses.after: when my steps were washed in curds and the rock poured out streams of oil for me!
verses.tsw_comparator: when my steps were washed with curds and the rock poured out streams of oil for me.

verses.rationale: Clarifies civic setting of remembered authority.
verses.before: When I went out to the gate of the city, when I prepared my seat in the square,
verses.after: When I went out to the city gate and took my seat in the square,
verses.tsw_comparator: When I went out to the gate of the city, when I prepared my seat in the square,

verses.rationale: Differentiates younger withdrawal and elders’ standing honor.
verses.before: young men saw me and withdrew, and the aged rose and stood.
verses.after: young men saw me and stepped aside; the aged rose and remained standing.
verses.tsw_comparator: young men saw me and withdrew, and the aged rose and stood.

verses.rationale: Keeps gesture rather than merely saying silence.
verses.before: Princes restrained their words and placed a hand over their mouth.
verses.after: Officials stopped talking and put their hands over their mouths.
verses.tsw_comparator: Princes restrained their words and placed a hand over their mouth.

verses.rationale: Retains striking bodily picture of respect.
verses.before: The voice of nobles was hushed, and their tongue clung to the roof of their mouth.
verses.after: The voices of nobles fell silent; their tongues clung to the roofs of their mouths.
verses.tsw_comparator: The voice of nobles was hushed, and their tongue clung to the roof of their mouth.

verses.rationale: Connects hearing and seeing with public testimony.
verses.before: For the ear that heard blessed me, and the eye that saw testified for me,
verses.after: Those who heard me called me blessed; those who saw me spoke in my favor,
verses.tsw_comparator: For the ear that heard blessed me, and the eye that saw testified for me,

verses.rationale: Names vulnerability and absence of support.
verses.before: because I delivered the poor who cried out, and the fatherless who had no helper.
verses.after: because I rescued the poor who cried for help and the orphan who had no helper.
verses.tsw_comparator: because I delivered the poor who cried out, and the fatherless who had no helper.

verses.rationale: Preserves blessing and emotional restoration.
verses.before: The blessing of the one about to perish came upon me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.
verses.after: The dying gave me their blessing; I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: The blessing of the one about to perish came upon me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.

verses.rationale: Keeps reciprocal clothing and paired garments.
verses.before: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; my justice was like a robe and a turban.
verses.after: I clothed myself with righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and turban.
verses.tsw_comparator: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; my justice was like a robe and a turban.

verses.rationale: Retains brief embodied parallel without forced variation.
verses.before: I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
verses.after: I was eyes for the blind and feet for the lame.
verses.tsw_comparator: I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.

verses.rationale: Reads unknown litigant; alternative unknown case noted.
verses.before: I was a father to the poor, and I investigated the case of one I did not know.
verses.after: I was a father to the needy; I investigated the case of someone I did not know.
verses.tsw_comparator: I was a father to the poor, and I investigated the case of one I did not know.

verses.rationale: Preserves violent predator image for rescue.
verses.before: I broke the jaws of the unjust and plucked the prey from his teeth.
verses.after: I broke the jaws of the unjust and pulled their prey from their teeth.
verses.tsw_comparator: I broke the jaws of the unjust and plucked the prey from his teeth.

verses.rationale: Follows sand reading while noting phoenix possibility.
verses.before: Then I said, ‘I will die in my nest, and multiply my days like the sand.
verses.after: I thought, ‘I will die in my nest, my days as numerous as sand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said, ‘I will die in my nest, and multiply my days like the sand.

verses.rationale: Keeps rooted plant image within hoped-for future.
verses.before: My root is open to the waters, and dew spends the night upon my branch.
verses.after: My roots will reach the water; dew will rest all night on my branches.
verses.tsw_comparator: My root is open to the waters, and dew spends the night upon my branch.

verses.rationale: Retains honor renewal and restored bow.
verses.before: My glory is fresh with me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.’
verses.after: My honor will remain fresh, and the bow in my hand will regain its strength.’
verses.tsw_comparator: My glory is fresh with me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.’

verses.rationale: Makes audience’s attentive waiting clear.
verses.before: People listened to me and waited; they were silent for my counsel.
verses.after: People listened to me and waited, keeping silent for my counsel.
verses.tsw_comparator: People listened to me and waited; they were silent for my counsel.

verses.rationale: Preserves speech falling as moisture into next image.
verses.before: After my word they did not speak again, and my speech dropped upon them.
verses.after: After I spoke, they said no more; my words fell gently on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: After my word they did not speak again, and my speech dropped upon them.

verses.rationale: Keeps rain longing and open mouths.
verses.before: They waited for me as for rain and opened their mouth for the spring rain.
verses.after: They waited for me as for rain, opening their mouths for the spring showers.
verses.tsw_comparator: They waited for me as for rain and opened their mouth for the spring rain.

verses.rationale: Selects uncertain confidence reading, preserves face-light clause.
verses.before: I smiled upon them when they did not believe it, and they did not cast down the light of my face.
verses.after: I smiled at them when they lacked confidence; they did not cast down the light of my face.
verses.tsw_comparator: I smiled upon them when they did not believe it, and they did not cast down the light of my face.

verses.rationale: Retains both leadership and mourner-comfort images.
verses.before: I chose their way and sat as chief; I lived like a king among his troops, like one who comforts mourners.”
verses.after: I chose their course and sat as their head, living like a king among his troops, like one who comforts mourners.
verses.tsw_comparator: I chose their way and sat as chief; I lived like a king among his troops, like one who comforts mourners.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Job’s contempt rather than sanitizing his voice.
verses.before: “But now they laugh at me, men younger than I, whose fathers I would have refused to put with the dogs of my flock.
verses.after: But now men younger than I am laugh at me, men whose fathers I disdained to put even with the dogs of my flock.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But now they laugh at me, men younger than I, whose fathers I would have refused to put with the dogs of my flock.

verses.rationale: Keeps dismissive question and exhausted strength.
verses.before: What use was the strength of their hands to me, when their vigor had perished?
verses.after: What use was the strength of their hands to me? Their vigor had deserted them.
verses.tsw_comparator: What use was the strength of their hands to me, when their vigor had perished?

verses.rationale: Retains difficult barren night image with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: Through want and hunger they were gaunt, gnawing the dry ground in darkness and desolation.
verses.after: Gaunt from want and hunger, they gnawed the dry ground in the night of waste and desolation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Through want and hunger they were gaunt, gnawing the dry ground in darkness and desolation.

verses.rationale: Preserves harsh foraging rather than modern diet explanation.
verses.before: They plucked salt herbs among the bushes, and the roots of broom trees were their food.
verses.after: They gathered salt plants among the bushes; broom roots were their food.
verses.tsw_comparator: They plucked salt herbs among the bushes, and the roots of broom trees were their food.

verses.rationale: Keeps social exclusion in Job’s description.
verses.before: They were driven out from the community; people shouted after them as after a thief.
verses.after: They were driven out from the community; people shouted at them as at a thief.
verses.tsw_comparator: They were driven out from the community; people shouted after them as after a thief.

verses.rationale: Preserves three rough dwelling images.
verses.before: They had to live in dreadful ravines, in holes of the earth and rocks.
verses.after: They had to live in the gullies, in holes in the earth and among rocks.
verses.tsw_comparator: They had to live in dreadful ravines, in holes of the earth and rocks.

verses.rationale: Keeps dehumanizing sound as Job’s rhetoric.
verses.before: Among the bushes they brayed; under nettles they huddled together.
verses.after: They brayed among the bushes and huddled beneath nettles.
verses.tsw_comparator: Among the bushes they brayed; under nettles they huddled together.

verses.rationale: Preserves status contempt and coercive expulsion.
verses.before: Children of fools, even children without a name, they were whipped out of the land.
verses.after: Children of fools, children without a name, they were beaten out of the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Children of fools, even children without a name, they were whipped out of the land.

verses.rationale: Links now-reversal to mockery’s two forms.
verses.before: And now I have become their song; I have become a byword to them.
verses.after: And now I have become their song; I am a byword among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now I have become their song; I have become a byword to them.

verses.rationale: Makes indignity explicit without euphemism.
verses.before: They abhor me and keep far from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
verses.after: They loathe me and keep their distance; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
verses.tsw_comparator: They abhor me and keep far from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.

verses.rationale: Follows read my string; names God as inferred subject.
verses.before: Because God has loosened my bowstring and humbled me, they cast off restraint before me.
verses.after: Because God has loosened my bowstring and humbled me, they have thrown off restraint in my presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because God has loosened my bowstring and humbled me, they cast off restraint before me.

verses.rationale: Retains obscure rabble and siege-road imagery.
verses.before: At my right hand a brood rises; they push away my feet and build their roads of destruction against me.
verses.after: The rabble rises at my right hand; they push my feet aside and build their roads of destruction against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: At my right hand a brood rises; they push away my feet and build their roads of destruction against me.

verses.rationale: Keeps difficult final clause rather than inventing restraint.
verses.before: They tear up my path; they profit from my calamity, with no one to restrain them.
verses.after: They tear up my path and advance my ruin, with no one to help them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They tear up my path; they profit from my calamity, with no one to restrain them.

verses.rationale: Carries siege image through invasion.
verses.before: As through a wide breach they come; amid the ruin they roll upon me.
verses.after: They come through as through a wide breach; amid the wreckage they roll in.
verses.tsw_comparator: As through a wide breach they come; amid the ruin they roll upon me.

verses.rationale: Preserves dignity and passing-cloud loss.
verses.before: Terrors are turned upon me; they pursue my dignity like the wind, and my salvation passes away like a cloud.
verses.after: Terrors turn upon me; my dignity is swept away like wind, and my deliverance passes like a cloud.
verses.tsw_comparator: Terrors are turned upon me; they pursue my dignity like the wind, and my salvation passes away like a cloud.

verses.rationale: Retains poured life and affliction’s grip.
verses.before: And now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction seize me.
verses.after: Now my life pours out within me; days of affliction have taken hold of me.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction seize me.

verses.rationale: Reads gnawing pains while noting uncertain sinews sense.
verses.before: At night my bones are pierced within me, and my gnawing pains do not rest.
verses.after: Night pierces my bones; the pains that gnaw me never rest.
verses.tsw_comparator: At night my bones are pierced within me, and my gnawing pains do not rest.

verses.rationale: Keeps difficult garment comparison without false certainty.
verses.before: With great force my garment is disfigured; it binds me like the collar of my tunic.
verses.after: With great force my clothing is distorted; it binds me like the collar of my tunic.
verses.tsw_comparator: With great force my garment is disfigured; it binds me like the collar of my tunic.

verses.rationale: Retains descent into bodily degradation.
verses.before: He has thrown me into the mire, and I have become like dust and ashes.
verses.after: He has thrown me into the mud; I have become like dust and ashes.
verses.tsw_comparator: He has thrown me into the mire, and I have become like dust and ashes.

verses.rationale: Preserves turn to direct address and unanswered appeal.
verses.before: I cry to you, but you do not answer me; I stand, and you merely look at me.
verses.after: I cry to you for help, but you do not answer; I stand, and you merely look at me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I cry to you, but you do not answer me; I stand, and you merely look at me.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct accusation of divine cruelty.
verses.before: You have turned cruel toward me; with the might of your hand you persecute me.
verses.after: You have turned cruel toward me; you attack me with the strength of your hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have turned cruel toward me; with the might of your hand you persecute me.

verses.rationale: Selects storm reading of disputed final expression; note variants.
verses.before: You lift me to the wind; you make me ride upon it, and you dissolve me in the storm.
verses.after: You lift me onto the wind and make me ride it; you dissolve me in the storm.
verses.tsw_comparator: You lift me to the wind; you make me ride upon it, and you dissolve me in the storm.

verses.rationale: Preserves universal destination and house image.
verses.before: For I know that you will bring me to death, to the house appointed for all living.
verses.after: I know you will bring me to death, to the house appointed for everyone alive.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I know that you will bring me to death, to the house appointed for all living.

verses.rationale: Marks difficult clause as appeal for ordinary help.
verses.before: Yet does not one stretch out a hand from a ruin? In disaster, does one not cry out for help?
verses.after: Does not a ruined person stretch out a hand, crying for help in his disaster?
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet does not one stretch out a hand from a ruin? In disaster, does one not cry out for help?

verses.rationale: Retains Job’s appeal to his former compassion.
verses.before: Did I not weep for the one whose day was hard? Was not my soul grieved for the poor?
verses.after: Did I not weep for those whose days were hard? Did my soul not grieve for the needy?
verses.tsw_comparator: Did I not weep for the one whose day was hard? Was not my soul grieved for the poor?

verses.rationale: Preserves balanced frustrated expectation.
verses.before: But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I waited for light, darkness came.
verses.after: Yet when I hoped for good, evil came; when I waited for light, darkness came.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I waited for light, darkness came.

verses.rationale: Keeps visceral unrest and attacking days.
verses.before: My inward parts churn and do not rest; days of affliction confront me.
verses.after: My insides seethe and never grow still; days of affliction confront me.
verses.tsw_comparator: My inward parts churn and do not rest; days of affliction confront me.

verses.rationale: Retains darkened body with alternative mourning noted.
verses.before: I walk darkened, but not by the sun; I rise in the assembly and cry for help.
verses.after: I walk about darkened, though not by the sun; I rise in the assembly and cry for help.
verses.tsw_comparator: I walk darkened, but not by the sun; I rise in the assembly and cry for help.

verses.rationale: Preserves animal kinship and lament sounds.
verses.before: I have become a brother to jackals and a companion to ostriches.
verses.after: I have become a brother to jackals, a companion to ostriches.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have become a brother to jackals and a companion to ostriches.

verses.rationale: Makes bodily suffering concrete, not metaphor alone.
verses.before: My skin turns black upon me, and my bones burn from heat.
verses.after: My skin blackens and peels from me; my bones burn with heat.
verses.tsw_comparator: My skin turns black upon me, and my bones burn from heat.

verses.rationale: Retains paired instruments and changed emotional register.
verses.before: My lyre has become mourning, and my pipe the voice of people who weep.”
verses.after: My lyre has turned to mourning, my pipe to the sound of weeping.
verses.tsw_comparator: My lyre has become mourning, and my pipe the voice of those who weep.”

verses.rationale: Keeps covenant and specific woman in the oath.
verses.before: “I made a covenant with my eyes; how then could I gaze upon a young woman?
verses.after: I made a covenant with my eyes; how, then, could I gaze at a young virgin?
verses.tsw_comparator: “I made a covenant with my eyes; how then could I gaze upon a young woman?

verses.rationale: Connects conduct to the repeated portion/inheritance image.
verses.before: For what is the portion from God above, or the inheritance from the Almighty on high?
verses.after: What portion would God above allot me, what inheritance would the Almighty send from on high?
verses.tsw_comparator: For what is the portion from God above, or the inheritance from the Almighty on high?

verses.rationale: Retains Job’s expectation without narrator endorsement.
verses.before: Is not calamity for the unjust and disaster for workers of harm?
verses.after: Is not disaster for the unjust, and calamity for those who do wrong?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is not calamity for the unjust and disaster for workers of harm?

verses.rationale: Preserves scrutiny now invoked for vindication.
verses.before: Does he not see my ways and count all my steps?
verses.after: Does he not see my ways and count every step I take?
verses.tsw_comparator: Does he not see my ways and count all my steps?

verses.rationale: Keeps oath condition interrupted by appeal.
verses.before: If I have walked with falsehood or my foot hurried toward deceit,
verses.after: If I have walked with falsehood and my feet have hurried toward deceit—
verses.tsw_comparator: If I have walked with falsehood or my foot hurried toward deceit,

verses.rationale: Retains scales and central integrity claim.
verses.before: let him weigh me in honest scales, and let God know my integrity.
verses.after: let God weigh me on honest scales and recognize my integrity—
verses.tsw_comparator: let him weigh me in honest scales, and let God know my integrity.

verses.rationale: Preserves three bodily images of wrongdoing.
verses.before: If my step has turned from the way, if my heart has gone after my eyes, or if any stain has clung to my hands,
verses.after: if my steps have strayed from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes, or any stain has clung to my hands,
verses.tsw_comparator: If my step has turned from the way, if my heart has gone after my eyes, or if any stain has clung to my hands,

verses.rationale: Retains agricultural curse; offspring alternative noted.
verses.before: then let me sow and another eat, and let my crops be uprooted.
verses.after: then let another eat what I sow, and let what grows for me be uprooted.
verses.tsw_comparator: then let me sow and another eat, and let my crops be uprooted.

verses.rationale: Keeps sexual and neighbor-specific offense.
verses.before: If my heart was enticed by a woman, or I lay in wait at my neighbor’s door,
verses.after: If my heart has been enticed by a woman and I have lurked at my neighbor’s door,
verses.tsw_comparator: If my heart was enticed by a woman, or I lay in wait at my neighbor’s door,

verses.rationale: Preserves disturbing curse and sexual implication without endorsement.
verses.before: then let my wife grind for another, and let others bow down over her.
verses.after: then let my wife grind for another man, and let other men bend over her.
verses.tsw_comparator: then let my wife grind for another, and let others bow down over her.

verses.rationale: Connects offense to adjudication rather than vague immorality.
verses.before: For that would be a disgraceful thing; it would be guilt for the judges.
verses.after: For that would be an outrage, an offense calling for judgment.
verses.tsw_comparator: For that would be a disgraceful thing; it would be guilt for the judges.

verses.rationale: Keeps destructive fire and death-realm endpoint.
verses.before: For it is a fire that consumes as far as Abaddon, and it would uproot all my produce.
verses.after: It would be a fire consuming as far as Abaddon, uprooting everything I produce.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is a fire that consumes as far as Abaddon, and it would uproot all my produce.

verses.rationale: Names enslaved status and both genders’ legal claim.
verses.before: If I rejected the case of my male servant or my female servant when they contended with me,
verses.after: If I rejected the just claim of my male or female slave when they brought a case against me,
verses.tsw_comparator: If I rejected the case of my male servant or my female servant when they contended with me,

verses.rationale: Makes divine investigation’s consequence clear.
verses.before: what then would I do when God rises? When he visits, what would I answer him?
verses.after: what would I do when God rose up? What answer could I give when he called me to account?
verses.tsw_comparator: what then would I do when God rises? When he visits, what would I answer him?

verses.rationale: Retains shared creation as basis for answering slave’s claim.
verses.before: Did not the one who made me in the womb make him? Did not one form us both in the womb?
verses.after: Did not the one who made me in the womb make him too? Did not the same one form us in the womb?
verses.tsw_comparator: Did not the one who made me in the womb make him? Did not one form us both in the womb?

verses.rationale: Preserves desire and disappointed eyes in conditional oath.
verses.before: If I withheld the poor from their desire, or caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
verses.after: If I withheld what the poor desired or let a widow’s eyes fail,
verses.tsw_comparator: If I withheld the poor from their desire, or caused the eyes of the widow to fail,

verses.rationale: Keeps concrete shared bread and unfinished condition.
verses.before: or ate my morsel alone and the fatherless did not eat from it—
verses.after: if I ate my bread alone and did not share it with the orphan—
verses.tsw_comparator: or ate my morsel alone and the fatherless did not eat from it—

verses.rationale: Retains difficult pronoun sequence and lifelong hyperbole.
verses.before: for from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow—
verses.after: though from my youth I raised him like a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow—
verses.tsw_comparator: for from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow—

verses.rationale: Preserves danger and lack of covering.
verses.before: if I saw anyone perishing for lack of clothing, or a needy person without covering,
verses.after: if I saw someone perishing for lack of clothing, a needy person with nothing to cover him,
verses.tsw_comparator: if I saw anyone perishing for lack of clothing, or a needy person without covering,

verses.rationale: Reads loins as body and retains bodily blessing.
verses.before: if his loins did not bless me, and he was not warmed with the fleece of my sheep,
verses.after: if his body did not bless me for warming him with wool from my sheep,
verses.tsw_comparator: if his loins did not bless me, and he was not warmed with the fleece of my sheep,

verses.rationale: Makes civic backing for oppression explicit.
verses.before: if I raised my hand against the fatherless because I saw my help in the gate,
verses.after: if I raised my hand against an orphan because I knew I had support at the gate,
verses.tsw_comparator: if I raised my hand against the fatherless because I saw my help in the gate,

verses.rationale: Preserves self-curse’s bodily violence.
verses.before: then let my shoulder fall from its socket, and let my arm be broken from its joint.
verses.after: then let my shoulder fall from its socket and my arm break from its joint!
verses.tsw_comparator: then let my shoulder fall from its socket, and let my arm be broken from its joint.

verses.rationale: Keeps fear as Job’s stated restraint.
verses.before: For calamity from God was terror to me, and because of his majesty I could not do such things.
verses.after: For God’s disaster terrified me; I could not stand before his majesty.
verses.tsw_comparator: For calamity from God was terror to me, and because of his majesty I could not do such things.

verses.rationale: Preserves direct address to wealth.
verses.before: If I made gold my confidence or said to fine gold, ‘You are my security,’
verses.after: If I made gold my confidence or said to fine gold, ‘You are my security,’
verses.tsw_comparator: If I made gold my confidence or said to fine gold, ‘You are my security,’

verses.rationale: Keeps abundance and personal acquisition as temptation.
verses.before: if I rejoiced because my wealth was great and because my hand had found much,
verses.after: if I rejoiced because my wealth was great, because my hands had gained so much,
verses.tsw_comparator: if I rejoiced because my wealth was great and because my hand had found much,

verses.rationale: Reads light as sun in celestial pair.
verses.before: if I saw the sun when it shone or the moon walking in splendor,
verses.after: if I looked at the shining sun or the moon moving in its splendor,
verses.tsw_comparator: if I saw the sun when it shone or the moon walking in splendor,

verses.rationale: Clarifies kissing gesture without inventing a named cult.
verses.before: and my heart was secretly enticed and my hand kissed my mouth,
verses.after: and my heart was secretly enticed, and my mouth kissed my hand in homage,
verses.tsw_comparator: and my heart was secretly enticed and my hand kissed my mouth,

verses.rationale: Retains judicial and divine allegiance consequences.
verses.before: this also would be guilt for the judges, for I would have denied God above.
verses.after: that too would be an offense calling for judgment, for I would have denied God above.
verses.tsw_comparator: this also would be guilt for the judges, for I would have denied God above.

verses.rationale: Keeps conditional denial of revenge pleasure.
verses.before: If I rejoiced at the ruin of the one who hated me or exulted when evil found him—
verses.after: If I rejoiced at my enemy’s ruin or exulted when evil overtook him—
verses.tsw_comparator: If I rejoiced at the ruin of the one who hated me or exulted when evil found him—

verses.rationale: Retains parenthetic denial and lethal curse.
verses.before: I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse—
verses.after: I have not let my mouth sin by calling down a curse on his life—
verses.tsw_comparator: I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse—

verses.rationale: Clarifies household testimony to generosity.
verses.before: if the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who has not been satisfied with his meat?’
verses.after: if the people of my tent did not say, ‘Who has not had his fill of Job’s meat?’—
verses.tsw_comparator: if the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who has not been satisfied with his meat?’

verses.rationale: Keeps concrete hospitality toward outsider.
verses.before: The resident alien did not spend the night outside; I opened my doors to the traveler.
verses.after: no stranger spent the night outside; I opened my doors to the traveler—
verses.tsw_comparator: The resident alien did not spend the night outside; I opened my doors to the traveler.

verses.rationale: Selects human comparison; Adam alternative noted.
verses.before: If I covered my transgressions like Adam, hiding my guilt in my bosom,
verses.after: if I concealed my rebellion as people do, hiding my wrongdoing in my bosom,
verses.tsw_comparator: If I covered my transgressions like Adam, hiding my guilt in my bosom,

verses.rationale: Preserves suspended oath and fear of social disgrace.
verses.before: because I feared a great crowd and the contempt of clans terrified me, so that I kept silent and did not go outside—
verses.after: because I feared the crowd and the clans’ contempt terrified me, so that I kept silent and did not go out the door—
verses.tsw_comparator: because I feared a great crowd and the contempt of clans terrified me, so that I kept silent and did not go outside—

verses.rationale: Retains legal climax and written mark.
verses.before: If only I had someone to hear me! Look, here is my mark. Let the Almighty answer me! Let my accuser write the indictment!
verses.after: if only someone would hear me! Here is my signature; let the Almighty answer me! Let my accuser put his indictment in writing!
verses.tsw_comparator: If only I had someone to hear me! Look, here is my mark. Let the Almighty answer me! Let my accuser write the indictment!

verses.rationale: Keeps surprising honor shown to indictment.
verses.before: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; I would bind it upon myself like a crown.
verses.after: I would carry it on my shoulder and bind it on myself like a crown.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; I would bind it upon myself like a crown.

verses.rationale: Retains fearless accounting and princely approach.
verses.before: I would declare to him the number of my steps; like a prince I would approach him.
verses.after: I would account for every step I have taken; I would approach him like a prince.
verses.tsw_comparator: I would declare to him the number of my steps; like a prince I would approach him.

verses.rationale: Preserves land as witness within renewed oath.
verses.before: If my land has cried out against me and its furrows have wept together,
verses.after: If my land cried out against me and its furrows wept together,
verses.tsw_comparator: If my land has cried out against me and its furrows have wept together,

verses.rationale: Keeps withheld payment and possible killing explicit.
verses.before: if I have eaten its strength without payment or caused the life of its owners to breathe out,
verses.after: if I ate its yield without paying or caused its owners to breathe their last,
verses.tsw_comparator: if I have eaten its strength without payment or caused the life of its owners to breathe out,

verses.rationale: Retains crop-specific curse and narrator’s formal closure.
verses.before: then let thorns grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.
verses.after: then let thorns grow instead of wheat and foul weeds instead of barley.” The words of Job were ended.
verses.tsw_comparator: then let thorns grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.

verses.rationale: Preserves narrator’s stated reason for their silence.
verses.before: Then these three men stopped answering Job because he was righteous in his own eyes.
verses.after: These three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then these three men stopped answering Job because he was righteous in his own eyes.

verses.rationale: Keeps genealogy and comparative claim behind anger.
verses.before: But the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, from the clan of Ram, burned against Job because he declared himself righteous rather than God.
verses.after: Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, became angry. He was angry with Job for declaring himself right rather than God.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, from the clan of Ram, burned against Job because he declared himself righteous rather than God.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned Job as condemned object.
verses.before: His anger also burned against his three friends because they had found no answer, yet they had condemned Job.
verses.after: He was also angry with Job’s three friends, because they had found no answer and yet had condemned Job.
verses.tsw_comparator: His anger also burned against his three friends because they had found no answer, yet they had condemned Job.

verses.rationale: Makes age-based deference clear.
verses.before: Now Elihu had waited for Job with words because they were older than he.
verses.after: Elihu had waited while Job spoke, because the others were older than he was.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Elihu had waited for Job with words because they were older than he.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated anger and speech exhaustion.
verses.before: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, his anger burned.
verses.after: But when Elihu saw that the three men had no answer left, his anger flared.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, his anger burned.

verses.rationale: Marks narrative-to-poetry transition inside verse paragraph.
verses.before: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said: “I am young in days, and you are aged; so I was timid and afraid to declare my knowledge to you.
verses.after: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite said: “I am young, and you are aged; that is why I held back, afraid to tell you what I know.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said: “I am young in days, and you are aged; therefore I was timid and afraid to declare my knowledge to you.

verses.rationale: Preserves quoted earlier conviction about age.
verses.before: I said, ‘Let days speak, and many years teach wisdom.’
verses.after: I thought, ‘Let age speak; let many years make wisdom known.’
verses.tsw_comparator: I said, ‘Let days speak, and many years teach wisdom.’

verses.rationale: Keeps spirit/breath parallel as Elihu’s alternative.
verses.before: But truly it is the spirit in a human, the breath of the Almighty, that gives them understanding.
verses.after: But it is the spirit within a mortal, the breath of the Almighty, that gives understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: But truly it is the spirit in a human, the breath of the Almighty, that gives them understanding.

verses.rationale: Renders great as age-contextual, noting alternative status sense.
verses.before: It is not the great who are wise, nor do the aged always understand justice.
verses.after: Many years do not make people wise, nor do the aged alone understand justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is not the great who are wise, nor do the aged always understand justice.

verses.rationale: Retains insistence on his turn.
verses.before: So I say, ‘Listen to me; I also will declare my knowledge.’
verses.after: So I say, ‘Listen to me; I too will tell you what I know.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me; I also will declare my knowledge.’

verses.rationale: Keeps waiting, listening, searching sequence.
verses.before: Look, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your understandings until you searched out what to say.
verses.after: I waited for your words, listened for your insights as you searched for what to say.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your understandings until you searched out what to say.

verses.rationale: Preserves failure to refute as distinct from silence.
verses.before: I gave you my attention, and look, there was no one who corrected Job, no one among you who answered his words.
verses.after: I gave you my attention, but none of you refuted Job or answered his words.
verses.tsw_comparator: I gave you my attention, and look, there was no one who corrected Job, no one among you who answered his words.

verses.rationale: Keeps warning against passing the argument to God.
verses.before: Do not say, ‘We have found wisdom; God will drive him away, not a man.’
verses.after: Do not say, ‘We have found wisdom; God must defeat him, not a human.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not say, ‘We have found wisdom; God will drive him away, not a man.’

verses.rationale: Names Job for intelligible relationship.
verses.before: He did not arrange his words against me, and I will not answer him with your speeches.
verses.after: Job has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did not arrange his words against me, and I will not answer him with your speeches.

verses.rationale: Retains third-person shift in Elihu’s address.
verses.before: They are dismayed; they answer no more; words have departed from them.
verses.after: They are dismayed and answer no more; words have deserted them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are dismayed; they answer no more; words have departed from them.

verses.rationale: Selects rhetorical question from compressed syntax.
verses.before: And will I wait because they do not speak, because they stand there and answer no more?
verses.after: Must I wait because they do not speak, because they stand there without another answer?
verses.tsw_comparator: And shall I wait because they do not speak, because they stand there and answer no more?

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated self-assertion.
verses.before: I also will answer my share; I also will declare my knowledge.
verses.after: I too will give my answer; I too will tell what I know.
verses.tsw_comparator: I also will answer my share; I also will declare my knowledge.

verses.rationale: Preserves inward pressure and spirit language.
verses.before: For I am full of words; the spirit within me constrains me.
verses.after: For I am full of words; the spirit within me presses hard.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I am full of words; the spirit within me constrains me.

verses.rationale: Retains new wineskins rather than harmonizing another image.
verses.before: Look, my belly is like wine with no vent; like new wineskins it is ready to burst.
verses.after: My belly is like wine with no vent, like new wineskins ready to burst.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, my belly is like wine with no vent; like new wineskins it is ready to burst.

verses.rationale: Makes relief-seeking speech audible.
verses.before: I will speak so that I may find relief; I will open my lips and answer.
verses.after: I must speak to find relief; I must open my lips and answer.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will speak so that I may find relief; I will open my lips and answer.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired refusals of partiality and flattery.
verses.before: Please let me not show partiality to anyone, and let me not flatter any human.
verses.after: I will show no one favoritism and flatter no human being.
verses.tsw_comparator: Please let me not show partiality to anyone, and let me not flatter any human.

verses.rationale: Retains threatened removal as motive.
verses.before: For I do not know how to flatter; if I did, my Maker would soon carry me away.”
verses.after: For I do not know how to flatter; my Maker would soon carry me away.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I do not know how to flatter; if I did, my Maker would soon carry me away.”

verses.rationale: Marks direct address within continuing speech.
verses.before: “But now, Job, please hear my speech, and give ear to all my words.
verses.after: But now, Job, listen to my words; pay attention to everything I say.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But now, Job, please hear my speech, and give ear to all my words.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily self-introduction without embellishment.
verses.before: Look, now I open my mouth; my tongue speaks in my palate.
verses.after: I have opened my mouth; my tongue is speaking within it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, now I open my mouth; my tongue speaks in my palate.

verses.rationale: Selects sincerity sense in difficult parallel.
verses.before: My words come from the uprightness of my heart, and my lips speak knowledge clearly.
verses.after: My words come from an upright heart; my lips speak sincerely what they know.
verses.tsw_comparator: My words come from the uprightness of my heart, and my lips speak knowledge clearly.

verses.rationale: Retains spirit and breath without doctrinal expansion.
verses.before: The Spirit of God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
verses.after: God’s spirit made me; the Almighty’s breath gives me life.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Spirit of God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.

verses.rationale: Keeps legal challenge’s ordered actions.
verses.before: If you can, answer me; arrange yourself before me; take your stand.
verses.after: Answer me if you can; set out your case before me and take your stand.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you can, answer me; arrange yourself before me; take your stand.

verses.rationale: Makes shared creaturely standing clear.
verses.before: Look, I am like you before God; I also was pinched from clay.
verses.after: Before God I am just like you; I too was shaped from clay.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am like you before God; I also was pinched from clay.

verses.rationale: Retains rare pressure term with transparent sense.
verses.before: Look, no terror of me should frighten you, and my pressure will not be heavy upon you.
verses.after: No terror of me need frighten you; my pressure will not weigh heavily on you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, no terror of me should frighten you, and my pressure will not be heavy upon you.

verses.rationale: Signals reported speech, not narrator’s summary endorsement.
verses.before: Surely you have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard the sound of your words:
verses.after: You said it in my hearing; I heard the sound of your words:
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely you have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard the sound of your words:

verses.rationale: Keeps Elihu’s portrayal of Job’s claim.
verses.before: ‘I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, and there is no guilt in me.
verses.after: ‘I am pure, without rebellion; I am clean, with no wrongdoing in me.
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, and there is no guilt in me.

verses.rationale: Names God in embedded complaint for clarity.
verses.before: Look, he finds occasions against me; he considers me his enemy.
verses.after: Yet God finds grounds to oppose me; he counts me as his enemy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, he finds occasions against me; he considers me his enemy.

verses.rationale: Preserves confinement and surveillance images.
verses.before: He puts my feet in the stocks; he watches all my paths.’
verses.after: He puts my feet in the stocks and watches every path I take.’
verses.tsw_comparator: He puts my feet in the stocks; he watches all my paths.’

verses.rationale: Keeps Elihu’s verdict and stated reason.
verses.before: Look, in this you are not right, I answer you, for God is greater than a human.
verses.after: Here, I answer you, you are not right, for God is greater than a mortal.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, in this you are not right, I answer you, for God is greater than a human.

verses.rationale: Selects God’s deeds reading; unanswered speech alternative noted.
verses.before: Why do you contend against him because he does not answer all a person’s words?
verses.after: Why do you dispute with him for not accounting for everything he does?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you contend against him because he does not answer all a person’s words?

verses.rationale: Makes repeated divine speech and human failure distinct.
verses.before: For God speaks in one way, and in two, though a person does not perceive it:
verses.after: God speaks in one way, then another, though people do not perceive it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For God speaks in one way, and in two, though a person does not perceive it:

verses.rationale: Preserves dream scene and successive temporal clauses.
verses.before: in a dream, a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls upon people, in slumber upon the bed.
verses.after: In a dream, a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people as they slumber in their beds,
verses.tsw_comparator: in a dream, a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls upon people, in slumber upon the bed.

verses.rationale: Retains opening and sealing paired images.
verses.before: Then he opens the ears of people and seals their instruction,
verses.after: then he opens their ears and seals his warning upon them,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he opens the ears of people and seals their instruction,

verses.rationale: Does not add evil where action itself is general.
verses.before: to turn a person from his deed and hide pride from a man,
verses.after: to turn a person from his course and keep pride from a man,
verses.tsw_comparator: to turn a person from his deed and hide pride from a man,

verses.rationale: Retains difficult weapon image, alternative channel noted.
verses.before: to hold back his life from the pit and his life from passing over by the weapon.
verses.after: to hold his life back from the pit, to keep him from crossing into death by the weapon.
verses.tsw_comparator: to hold back his life from the pit and his life from passing over by the weapon.

verses.rationale: Combines bone-totality reading with enduring pain.
verses.before: A person is corrected with pain upon his bed and with continual strife in his bones,
verses.after: Or a person is corrected by pain on his bed, with unceasing anguish in all his bones,
verses.tsw_comparator: A person is corrected with pain upon his bed and with continual strife in his bones,

verses.rationale: Makes appetite loss clear while retaining paired foods.
verses.before: so that his life loathes bread and his soul desirable food.
verses.after: until his life loathes bread and his appetite rejects even desirable food.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that his life loathes bread and his soul desirable food.

verses.rationale: Follows read protruding bones and visual reversal.
verses.before: His flesh wastes away from sight, and his bones once unseen stick out.
verses.after: His flesh wastes from sight; his bones, once unseen, protrude.
verses.tsw_comparator: His flesh wastes away from sight, and his bones once unseen stick out.

verses.rationale: Retains plural death-bringers without naming them angels.
verses.before: His life draws near to the pit, and his life to people who bring death.
verses.after: His life draws near the pit, his existence to those who bring death.
verses.tsw_comparator: His life draws near to the pit, and his life to those who bring death.

verses.rationale: Leaves messenger’s identity and interpretation open.
verses.before: If there is a messenger for him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to declare to a human what is upright for him,
verses.after: But if a messenger stands beside him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to tell a person what is right for him,
verses.tsw_comparator: If there is a messenger for him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to declare to a human what is upright for him,

verses.rationale: Keeps ambiguous subject without inserting God or Christ.
verses.before: then he is gracious to him and says, ‘Deliver him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom.’
verses.after: then he shows him mercy and says, ‘Spare him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom,’
verses.tsw_comparator: then he is gracious to him and says, ‘Deliver him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom.’

verses.rationale: Retains bodily renewal and restored youth.
verses.before: His flesh becomes fresher than in youth; he returns to the days of his youthful strength.
verses.after: his flesh grows fresh as a child’s; he returns to the days of his youthful strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: His flesh becomes fresher than in youth; he returns to the days of his youthful strength.

verses.rationale: Clarifies shifting subjects in restored relationship.
verses.before: He prays to God, and God accepts him; he sees God’s face with a joyful shout, and God restores to a human his righteousness.
verses.after: He prays to God, and God accepts him; he sees God’s face with a shout of joy, and God restores his right standing.
verses.tsw_comparator: He prays to God, and God accepts him; he sees God’s face with a joyful shout, and God restores to a human his righteousness.

verses.rationale: Selects singing and undeserved relief senses; alternatives noted.
verses.before: He sings before people and says, ‘I sinned and twisted what was right, and it was not repaid to me.
verses.after: He sings before others and says, ‘I sinned and twisted what was right, but I was not repaid as I deserved.’
verses.tsw_comparator: He sings before people and says, ‘I sinned and twisted what was right, and it was not repaid to me.

verses.rationale: Follows read third person rather than written first person.
verses.before: He redeemed my life from passing into the pit, and my life will see the light.’
verses.after: God has redeemed his life from crossing into the pit, and he will live to see the light.
verses.tsw_comparator: He redeemed my life from passing into the pit, and my life will see the light.’

verses.rationale: Preserves ascending repetition without fixed quota.
verses.before: Look, God does all these things twice, three times with a person,
verses.after: God does all these things twice, three times, with a person,
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, God does all these things twice, three times with a person,

verses.rationale: Keeps pit-to-light movement.
verses.before: to bring back his life from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life.
verses.after: to bring his life back from the pit, to shine on him with the light of the living.
verses.tsw_comparator: to bring back his life from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life.

verses.rationale: Retains imperative demands, not softened invitation.
verses.before: Pay attention, Job; listen to me. Be silent, and I will speak.
verses.after: Pay attention, Job; listen to me. Be silent, and I will speak.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pay attention, Job; listen to me. Be silent, and I will speak.

verses.rationale: Keeps professed desire for vindication.
verses.before: If you have words, answer me; speak, for I desire to justify you.
verses.after: If you have something to say, answer me. Speak, for I want to find you in the right.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you have words, answer me; speak, for I desire to justify you.

verses.rationale: Preserves forceful closing claim to teach.
verses.before: If not, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.”
verses.after: If not, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.”
verses.tsw_comparator: If not, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.”

verses.rationale: Marks renewed speech without new speaker.
verses.before: Elihu answered and said:
verses.after: Elihu went on:
verses.tsw_comparator: Elihu answered and said:

verses.rationale: Retains address to broader discerning audience.
verses.before: “Hear my words, you wise people; and you who know, give ear to me.
verses.after: “Hear my words, you wise people; you who know, listen to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Hear my words, you wise people; and you who know, give ear to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps recurring testing image from Job’s speech.
verses.before: For the ear tests words as the palate tastes food.
verses.after: For the ear tests words as the palate tastes food.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the ear tests words as the palate tastes food.

verses.rationale: Makes proposed joint assessment clear.
verses.before: Let us choose justice for ourselves; let us know among ourselves what is good.
verses.after: Let us decide together what is just; let us discover among ourselves what is good.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let us choose justice for ourselves; let us know among ourselves what is good.

verses.rationale: Signals Elihu’s quotation of Job.
verses.before: For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, but God has taken away my justice.
verses.after: For Job has said, ‘I am in the right, but God has denied me justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, but God has taken away my justice.

verses.rationale: Selects passive counted-liar reading with alternative note.
verses.before: In spite of my justice I am counted a liar; my wound is incurable, though I have no transgression.’
verses.after: Despite my right, I am counted a liar; my arrow wound is incurable, though I have not rebelled.’
verses.tsw_comparator: In spite of my justice I am counted a liar; my wound is incurable, though I have no transgression.’

verses.rationale: Preserves drinking metaphor and accusation.
verses.before: What man is like Job, who drinks mockery like water,
verses.after: Who is like Job, drinking mockery like water,
verses.tsw_comparator: What man is like Job, who drinks mockery like water,

verses.rationale: Keeps accusation as Elihu’s, not narrator’s fact.
verses.before: who travels in company with workers of harm and walks with wicked people?
verses.after: keeping company with evildoers and walking with wicked men?
verses.tsw_comparator: who travels in company with workers of harm and walks with wicked people?

verses.rationale: Retains paraphrased reported position without certifying exact quotation.
verses.before: For he has said, ‘It does not profit a man to delight himself in God.’
verses.after: For he says, ‘It does a person no good to take delight in God.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For he has said, ‘It does not profit a man to delight himself in God.’

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic paired rejection.
verses.before: So listen to me, people of understanding: far be it from God to do wickedness, and from the Almighty to do injustice.
verses.after: So listen to me, you people of understanding: God is far from wickedness, the Almighty from injustice!
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore listen to me, people of understanding: far be it from God to do wickedness, and from the Almighty to do injustice.

verses.rationale: Makes retribution principle clear as Elihu’s assertion.
verses.before: For the work of a human he repays him, and according to a person’s way he causes him to find.
verses.after: He repays people for what they do, bringing upon each the outcome of his ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the work of a human he repays him, and according to a person’s way he causes him to find.

verses.rationale: Retains repetition rather than compressing argument.
verses.before: Surely God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.
verses.after: Truly, God does no wrong; the Almighty does not twist justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.

verses.rationale: Preserves questions denying delegated divine authority.
verses.before: Who appointed him over the earth? And who placed the entire world under him?
verses.after: Who entrusted the earth to him? Who placed the whole inhabited world in his care?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who appointed him over the earth? And who placed the whole world under him?

verses.rationale: Leaves first pronoun open; retains withdrawn breath.
verses.before: If he set his heart upon himself, if he gathered to himself his spirit and his breath,
verses.after: If he set his heart on it and gathered his spirit and breath back to himself,
verses.tsw_comparator: If he set his heart upon himself, if he gathered to himself his spirit and his breath,

verses.rationale: Keeps comprehensive mortality and earth-return.
verses.before: all flesh would expire together, and humanity would return to dust.
verses.after: all flesh would perish together, and humanity would return to dust.
verses.tsw_comparator: all flesh would expire together, and humanity would return to dust.

verses.rationale: Retains renewed singular appeal.
verses.before: If you have understanding, hear this; give ear to the sound of my words.
verses.after: If you have understanding, hear this; listen to the sound of my words.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you have understanding, hear this; give ear to the sound of my words.

verses.rationale: Carries question into next verse’s description.
verses.before: Can one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the righteous and mighty One,
verses.after: Can one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the righteous and mighty one,
verses.tsw_comparator: Can one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the righteous and mighty One,

verses.rationale: Selects divine subject while noting alternative prohibition reading.
verses.before: who says to a king, ‘Worthless one,’ and to nobles, ‘Wicked,’
verses.after: who says to a king, ‘Worthless man!’ and to nobles, ‘Wicked men!’?
verses.tsw_comparator: who says to a king, ‘Worthless one,’ and to nobles, ‘Wicked,’

verses.rationale: Keeps shared creation as reason for impartiality.
verses.before: who does not show partiality to princes or recognize the rich above the poor, for all of them are the work of his hands?
verses.after: He shows no partiality to officials and does not favor the rich over the poor, for all are the work of his hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: who does not show partiality to princes or recognize the rich above the poor, for all of them are the work of his hands?

verses.rationale: Preserves suddenness, night, and unseen agency.
verses.before: In a moment they die, and at midnight a people is shaken and passes away; the mighty are removed, but not by human hand.
verses.after: In a moment they die; at midnight people are shaken and pass away. The mighty are removed without a human hand.
