verses.tsw_comparator: In a moment they die, and at midnight a people is shaken and passes away; the mighty are removed, but not by human hand.

verses.rationale: Retains scrutiny image repeated from Job’s oath.
verses.before: For his eyes are upon the ways of a person, and he sees all his steps.
verses.after: His eyes are on a person’s ways; he sees every step.
verses.tsw_comparator: For his eyes are upon the ways of a person, and he sees all his steps.

verses.rationale: Keeps parallel dark places and failed concealment.
verses.before: There is no darkness and no death-shadow where workers of harm may hide.
verses.after: There is no darkness, no deep shadow, where evildoers can hide.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is no darkness and no death-shadow where workers of harm may hide.

verses.rationale: Selects no-further-investigation reading; appointed time alternative noted.
verses.before: For he does not appoint a time for a man to enter before God in judgment.
verses.after: He has no need to examine a person further before bringing him into judgment with God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he does not appoint a time for a man to enter before God in judgment.

verses.rationale: Preserves sudden replacement and lack of investigation.
verses.before: He breaks mighty people without searching it out and makes others stand in their place.
verses.after: He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets others in their place.
verses.tsw_comparator: He breaks mighty people without searching it out and makes others stand in their place.

verses.rationale: Connects known conduct to nocturnal overthrow.
verses.before: So he recognizes their works; he overturns them in the night, and they are crushed.
verses.after: Knowing their deeds, he overturns them in the night, and they are crushed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore he recognizes their works; he overturns them in the night, and they are crushed.

verses.rationale: Keeps public visibility of judgment.
verses.before: He strikes them for their wickedness in a place where people can see,
verses.after: He strikes them as wicked people in a place where others can see,
verses.tsw_comparator: He strikes them for their wickedness in a place where people can see,

verses.rationale: Preserves two forms of departure.
verses.before: because they turned aside from following him and gave no attention to any of his ways,
verses.after: because they turned away from following him and paid no attention to his ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: because they turned aside from following him and gave no attention to any of his ways,

verses.rationale: Keeps oppressed voices and divine hearing.
verses.before: so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him, and he heard the cry of the afflicted.
verses.after: They made the cry of the poor reach him, and he hears the cry of the afflicted.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him, and he heard the cry of the afflicted.

verses.rationale: Selects quietness rather than guaranteeing political peace.
verses.before: When he gives quiet, who can condemn? When he hides his face, who can see him? Whether over a nation or over a person, it is the same,
verses.after: When he is quiet, who can condemn him? When he hides his face, who can see him? He is over nation and individual alike,
verses.tsw_comparator: When he gives quiet, who can condemn? When he hides his face, who can see him? Whether over a nation or over a person, it is the same,

verses.rationale: Connects difficult clause to protection from oppressive rule.
verses.before: so that a godless person may not reign, so that there are no snares for the people.
verses.after: to keep a godless person from ruling, from setting snares for the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that a godless person may not reign, so that there are no snares for the people.

verses.rationale: Makes hypothetical confession audible.
verses.before: For has anyone said to God, ‘I have borne chastisement; I will not act corruptly again.
verses.after: Suppose someone says to God, ‘I have borne punishment; I will offend no more.
verses.tsw_comparator: For has anyone said to God, ‘I have borne chastisement; I will not act corruptly again.

verses.rationale: Preserves request for instruction and conditional acknowledgment.
verses.before: What I do not see, teach me; if I have done injustice, I will do it no more’?
verses.after: Teach me what I do not see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.’
verses.tsw_comparator: What I do not see, teach me; if I have done injustice, I will do it no more’?

verses.rationale: Keeps challenging choice without resolving every ellipsis.
verses.before: Should he repay according to your terms because you reject his judgment? For you must choose, and not I. So declare what you know.
verses.after: Must God repay on your terms because you object? You must choose, not I. Say what you know.
verses.tsw_comparator: Should he repay according to your terms because you reject his judgment? For you must choose, and not I. So declare what you know.

verses.rationale: Preserves Elihu’s anticipated agreement.
verses.before: People of understanding will say to me, and a wise man who hears me:
verses.after: People of understanding will tell me, a wise man who hears me will say,
verses.tsw_comparator: People of understanding will say to me, and a wise man who hears me:

verses.rationale: Marks condemnation as quoted expected response.
verses.before: ‘Job speaks without knowledge, and his words are without insight.’
verses.after: ‘Job speaks without knowledge; his words show no insight.’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Job speaks without knowledge, and his words are without insight.’

verses.rationale: Preserves harsh wish and ambiguous opening with note.
verses.before: If only Job were tested to the limit because his answers are like those of wicked men!
verses.after: If only Job were tested to the limit for answering like evildoers!
verses.tsw_comparator: If only Job were tested to the limit because his answers are like those of wicked men!

verses.rationale: Retains accusation and dismissive gesture.
verses.before: For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.”
verses.after: He adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.”

verses.rationale: Keeps speech formula and sequence.
verses.before: Elihu answered and said:
verses.after: Elihu continued:
verses.tsw_comparator: Elihu answered and said:

verses.rationale: Chooses comparative reading while noting right-before-God alternative.
verses.before: “Do you think this is justice? You say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’
verses.after: “Do you think this is just? Do you say, ‘I am more righteous than God,’
verses.tsw_comparator: “Do you think this is justice? You say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’

verses.rationale: Retains pronoun shift in difficult reported question.
verses.before: for you ask, ‘What does it profit you? What do I gain by not sinning?’
verses.after: when you ask, ‘What use is it to you? What do I gain by not sinning?’
verses.tsw_comparator: for you ask, ‘What does it profit you? What do I gain by not sinning?’

verses.rationale: Keeps addressed group explicit.
verses.before: I will answer you and your friends with you.
verses.after: I will answer you and your friends along with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will answer you and your friends with you.

verses.rationale: Retains invitation to observe height.
verses.before: Look at the heavens and see; look the clouds, which are higher than you.
verses.after: Look up at the heavens and see; look at the clouds, high above you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look at the heavens and see; behold the clouds, which are higher than you.

verses.rationale: Keeps questions about divine harm, not moral permission.
verses.before: If you sin, what do you accomplish against him? If your transgressions multiply, what do you do to him?
verses.after: If you sin, what do you do to him? If your rebellions multiply, how do they affect him?
verses.tsw_comparator: If you sin, what do you accomplish against him? If your transgressions multiply, what do you do to him?

verses.rationale: Preserves gift-and-hand comparison.
verses.before: If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?
verses.after: If you are righteous, what do you give him? What does he receive from your hand?
verses.tsw_comparator: If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?

verses.rationale: Makes implied human effects explicit.
verses.before: Your wickedness affects a human like yourself, and your righteousness a son of man.
verses.after: Your wickedness affects a person like yourself, and your righteousness another human being.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your wickedness affects a human like yourself, and your righteousness a son of man.

verses.rationale: Keeps oppression and powerful arm image.
verses.before: Because of the multitude of oppressions people cry out; they call for help because of the arm of the mighty.
verses.after: People cry out under great oppression; they call for help beneath the arm of the powerful.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of the multitude of oppressions people cry out; they call for help because of the arm of the mighty.

verses.rationale: Preserves Elihu’s criticism of supplicants.
verses.before: But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
verses.after: But no one asks, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
verses.tsw_comparator: But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,

verses.rationale: Keeps comparative teaching, noting animal-instruction alternative.
verses.before: who teaches us more than the animals of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the heavens?’
verses.after: who teaches us more than the earth’s animals and makes us wiser than the birds of the heavens?’
verses.tsw_comparator: who teaches us more than the animals of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the heavens?’

verses.rationale: Leaves arrogance’s referent unforced.
verses.before: There they cry out, but he does not answer, because of the pride of evil people.
verses.after: There they cry out, but he does not answer, because of the arrogance of evil people.
verses.tsw_comparator: There they cry out, but he does not answer, because of the pride of evil people.

verses.rationale: Keeps forceful assertion belonging to Elihu.
verses.before: Surely God does not hear emptiness, and the Almighty does not regard it.
verses.after: Surely God does not listen to emptiness; the Almighty pays it no attention.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely God does not hear emptiness, and the Almighty does not regard it.

verses.rationale: Connects unseen God to continued legal appeal.
verses.before: How much less when you say you do not see him, that your case is before him and you must wait for him.
verses.after: How much less when you say you cannot see him! Your case is before him; wait for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: How much less when you say you do not see him, that your case is before him and you must wait for him.

verses.rationale: Selects difficult transgression sense; flags rare word.
verses.before: And now, because his anger has not visited and he does not greatly recognize arrogance,
verses.after: But now, because his anger has not punished and he has not taken much notice of transgression,
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, because his anger has not visited and he does not greatly recognize arrogance,

verses.rationale: Completes accusation’s causal movement.
verses.before: Job opens his mouth in emptiness; without knowledge he multiplies words.”
verses.after: Job opens his mouth in emptiness and multiplies words without knowledge.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Job opens his mouth in emptiness; without knowledge he multiplies words.”

verses.rationale: Retains continued speaker formula.
verses.before: Elihu continued and said:
verses.after: Elihu went on:
verses.tsw_comparator: Elihu continued and said:

verses.rationale: Keeps self-appointed advocacy explicit.
verses.before: “Wait for me a little, and I will show you, for there are still words for God.
verses.after: “Bear with me a little, and I will show you; there is still more to say on God’s behalf.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Wait for me a little, and I will show you, for there are still words for God.

verses.rationale: Retains distance image and asserted vindication.
verses.before: I will bring my knowledge from far away and give righteousness to my Maker.
verses.after: I will bring my knowledge from afar and ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will bring my knowledge from far away and give righteousness to my Maker.

verses.rationale: Preserves extraordinary self-claim without endorsement.
verses.before: For truly my words are not false; one complete in knowledge is with you.
verses.after: Truly, my words are not false; one complete in knowledge is with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For truly my words are not false; one complete in knowledge is with you.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated might and non-contempt.
verses.before: Look, God is mighty and does not reject; he is mighty in strength of heart.
verses.after: God is mighty, yet despises no one; he is mighty in strength of understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, God is mighty and does not reject; he is mighty in strength of heart.

verses.rationale: Preserves Elihu’s disputed retribution claim.
verses.before: He does not preserve the wicked alive, but gives justice to the afflicted.
verses.after: He does not keep the wicked alive; he grants justice to the afflicted.
verses.tsw_comparator: He does not preserve the wicked alive, but gives justice to the afflicted.

verses.rationale: Keeps royal elevation and enduring claim.
verses.before: He does not withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne he seats them forever, and they are exalted.
verses.after: He does not take his eyes off the righteous; he seats them with kings on thrones forever, and they are exalted.
verses.tsw_comparator: He does not withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne he seats them forever, and they are exalted.

verses.rationale: Retains conditional descent into confinement.
verses.before: And if they are bound in chains and caught in cords of affliction,
verses.after: But if they are bound in chains, caught in the cords of affliction,
verses.tsw_comparator: And if they are bound in chains and caught in cords of affliction,

verses.rationale: Keeps conduct and pride as Elihu’s explanation.
verses.before: then he declares to them their work and their transgressions, that they acted arrogantly.
verses.after: he tells them what they have done, their rebellions and their arrogance.
verses.tsw_comparator: then he declares to them their work and their transgressions, that they acted arrogantly.

verses.rationale: Retains opened-ear image as instruction.
verses.before: He opens their ear to discipline and commands that they turn back from harm.
verses.after: He opens their ears to correction and tells them to turn from wrongdoing.
verses.tsw_comparator: He opens their ear to discipline and commands that they turn back from harm.

verses.rationale: Preserves conditional promise rather than universal narrator claim.
verses.before: If they listen and serve him, they complete their days in prosperity and their years in pleasantness.
verses.after: If they listen and serve him, they finish their days in prosperity and their years in pleasantness.
verses.tsw_comparator: If they listen and serve him, they complete their days in prosperity and their years in pleasantness.

verses.rationale: Retains weapon/death and ignorance consequence.
verses.before: But if they do not listen, they pass away by the weapon and expire without knowledge.
verses.after: But if they do not listen, they pass away by the weapon and die without knowledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if they do not listen, they pass away by the weapon and expire without knowledge.

verses.rationale: Keeps inward resentment and refused appeal.
verses.before: The godless in heart store up anger; they do not cry for help when he binds them.
verses.after: The godless at heart store up anger; they do not cry for help when he binds them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The godless in heart store up anger; they do not cry for help when he binds them.

verses.rationale: Retains masculine cultic term without asserting disputed sexual role.
verses.before: Their life dies in youth, and their life among the cult prostitutes.
verses.after: They die in their youth; their life ends among the male shrine attendants.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their life dies in youth, and their life among the cult prostitutes.

verses.rationale: Keeps instrumental suffering claim as Elihu’s theology.
verses.before: He delivers the afflicted through their affliction and opens their ear through oppression.
verses.after: He rescues the afflicted through their affliction and opens their ears through oppression.
verses.tsw_comparator: He delivers the afflicted through their affliction and opens their ear through oppression.

verses.rationale: Retains mouth-to-open-space and table images.
verses.before: He also entices you from the mouth of distress to a broad place with no constraint, and what is set upon your table will be full of richness.
verses.after: He is drawing you too from distress’s jaws into a broad place with no confinement, to a table set with rich food.
verses.tsw_comparator: He also entices you from the mouth of distress to a broad place with no constraint, and what is set upon your table will be full of richness.

verses.rationale: Preserves difficult accusation and judicial pair.
verses.before: But you are filled with the judgment of the wicked; judgment and justice take hold of you.
verses.after: But you are full of the judgment due the wicked; judgment and justice take hold of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you are filled with the judgment of the wicked; judgment and justice take hold of you.

verses.rationale: Selects anger/mockery reading; wealth alternative noted.
verses.before: Beware lest wrath entice you into scoffing, and do not let the greatness of a ransom turn you aside.
verses.after: Beware that anger does not lure you into mockery; do not let a great ransom turn you aside.
verses.tsw_comparator: Beware lest wrath entice you into scoffing, and do not let the greatness of a ransom turn you aside.

verses.rationale: Keeps question and rare cry/wealth ambiguity.
verses.before: Will your wealth keep you from distress, or all the forces of your strength?
verses.after: Can your cry keep you out of distress, or all the force of your strength?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will your wealth keep you from distress, or all the forces of your strength?

verses.rationale: Preserves obscure warning without defining desired death.
verses.before: Do not long for the night, when peoples are removed from their place.
verses.after: Do not long for the night when peoples are swept from their places.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not long for the night, when peoples are removed from their place.

verses.rationale: Keeps Elihu’s allegation rather than softening advice.
verses.before: Take care; do not turn toward harm, for you have chosen this rather than affliction.
verses.after: Take care; do not turn to wrongdoing, for you have chosen it instead of affliction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take care; do not turn toward harm, for you have chosen this rather than affliction.

verses.rationale: Retains divine teacher image.
verses.before: Look, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?
verses.after: God is exalted in power. Who is a teacher like him?
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?

verses.rationale: Keeps questions of authority and accusation.
verses.before: Who has appointed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have done injustice’?
verses.after: Who has prescribed his course for him? Who has said, ‘You have done wrong’?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has appointed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have done injustice’?

verses.rationale: Preserves invitation to praise observed deeds.
verses.before: Remember to magnify his work, which people have sung.
verses.after: Remember to magnify his work, which people have celebrated in song.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember to magnify his work, which people have sung.

verses.rationale: Keeps universal sight and limited distance.
verses.before: All humanity has seen it; a mortal beholds it from far away.
verses.after: All humanity has seen it; mortals gaze on it from afar.
verses.tsw_comparator: All humanity has seen it; a mortal beholds it from far away.

verses.rationale: Preserves unknowability and immeasurable years.
verses.before: Look, God is great, and we do not know him; the number of his years cannot be searched out.
verses.after: God is great beyond our knowing; the number of his years cannot be searched out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, God is great, and we do not know him; the number of his years cannot be searched out.

verses.rationale: Keeps ancient water image with uncertain mist relation noted.
verses.before: For he draws up drops of water; they distill rain from his mist,
verses.after: He draws up drops of water; they distill his mist into rain,
verses.tsw_comparator: For he draws up drops of water; they distill rain from his mist,

verses.rationale: Preserves generous rainfall and human recipients.
verses.before: which the clouds pour down and drip upon humanity abundantly.
verses.after: which the clouds pour down and shower abundantly on people.
verses.tsw_comparator: which the clouds pour down and drip upon humanity abundantly.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine cloud-shelter imagery.
verses.before: Can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds, the thunderings of his pavilion?
verses.after: Can anyone understand the spreading clouds, the thunder from his shelter?
verses.tsw_comparator: Can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds, the thunderings of his pavilion?

verses.rationale: Retains difficult sea-roots image rather than normalizing weather.
verses.before: Look, he spreads his lightning around him and covers the roots of the sea.
verses.after: He spreads his light around him and covers the roots of the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, he spreads his lightning around him and covers the roots of the sea.

verses.rationale: Keeps storm’s judgment and nourishment together.
verses.before: For by these he judges peoples; he gives food in abundance.
verses.after: By these he judges peoples and gives food in abundance.
verses.tsw_comparator: For by these he judges peoples; he gives food in abundance.

verses.rationale: Selects hands-filled-lightning and striking sense.
verses.before: He covers his hands with lightning and commands it concerning the target.
verses.after: He covers his hands with lightning and commands it to strike its target.
verses.tsw_comparator: He covers his hands with lightning and commands it concerning the target.

verses.rationale: Flags highly uncertain cattle/approach wording in note.
verses.before: His thunder declares his presence; the cattle also declare what is coming.
verses.after: His thunder announces him; even the cattle tell of the storm’s approach.
verses.tsw_comparator: His thunder declares his presence; the cattle also declare what is coming.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily awe at storm.
verses.before: “At this also my heart trembles and leaps from its place.
verses.after: At this my heart trembles and leaps from its place.
verses.tsw_comparator: “At this also my heart trembles and leaps from its place.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated listening and divine speech image.
verses.before: Listen carefully to the thunder of his voice and the rumbling that goes out from his mouth.
verses.after: Listen closely to the thunder of his voice, the rumbling that comes from his mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Listen carefully to the thunder of his voice and the rumbling that goes out from his mouth.

verses.rationale: Keeps broad reach and earth’s extremities.
verses.before: Under all the heavens he sends it, and his lightning to the edges of the earth.
verses.after: He sends it beneath the whole sky, his lightning to the edges of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Under all the heavens he sends it, and his lightning to the edges of the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps sequence of lightning and thunder, ambiguous object unforced.
verses.before: After it a voice roars; he thunders with his majestic voice, and he does not hold back the flashes when his voice is heard.
verses.after: After it comes a roaring sound; he thunders with his majestic voice. He holds nothing back when his voice is heard.
verses.tsw_comparator: After it a voice roars; he thunders with his majestic voice, and he does not hold back the flashes when his voice is heard.

verses.rationale: Retains wonder and limited knowledge.
verses.before: God thunders wondrously with his voice; he does great things that we cannot know.
verses.after: God thunders wondrously with his voice; he does great things beyond our understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: God thunders wondrously with his voice; he does great things that we cannot know.

verses.rationale: Makes weather command’s ellipsis audible.
verses.before: For he says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ and to the rain shower, and to his mighty showers of rain.
verses.after: He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ and likewise to the downpour, his mighty rain.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ and to the rain shower, and to his mighty showers of rain.

verses.rationale: Retains sealed hands and purpose, alternative knowledge object noted.
verses.before: He seals the hand of every human, so that all people may know his work.
verses.after: He seals every human hand, so that all those he made may know his work.
verses.tsw_comparator: He seals the hand of every human, so that all people may know his work.

verses.rationale: Keeps animal shelter parallel to human stopped work.
verses.before: Then the animal enters its lair and remains in its den.
verses.after: The wild animal enters its den and stays in its dwelling.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the animal enters its lair and remains in its den.

verses.rationale: Retains uncertain wind designation without invented geography.
verses.before: From the chamber comes the storm, and cold from the scattering winds.
verses.after: The storm comes from its chamber, and cold from the scattering winds.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the chamber comes the storm, and cold from the scattering winds.

verses.rationale: Preserves breath and constrained water.
verses.before: By the breath of God ice is given, and the broad waters are frozen.
verses.after: God’s breath gives ice, and the broad waters freeze solid.
verses.tsw_comparator: By the breath of God ice is given, and the broad waters are frozen.

verses.rationale: Keeps cloud as laden and dispersed.
verses.before: He loads the thick cloud with moisture; the cloud scatters his lightning.
verses.after: He loads the clouds with moisture and scatters his lightning cloud.
verses.tsw_comparator: He loads the thick cloud with moisture; the cloud scatters his lightning.

verses.rationale: Follows read guidance plural in natural collective wording.
verses.before: It turns around and around by his guidance, to do all that he commands it on the face of the inhabited earth.
verses.after: They turn about under his direction, doing whatever he commands across the face of the inhabited earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: It turns around and around by his guidance, to do all that he commands it on the face of the inhabited earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves three purposes including difficult land phrase.
verses.before: Whether for a rod, or for his land, or for steadfast love, he causes it to find its mark.
verses.after: Whether for punishment, for his land, or for faithful love, he makes it happen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whether for a rod, or for his land, or for steadfast love, he causes it to find its mark.

verses.rationale: Names addressee and invites attention.
verses.before: Give ear to this, Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God.
verses.after: Listen to this, Job. Stand still and consider God’s wonders.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give ear to this, Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps questions of weather governance.
verses.before: Do you know how God appoints them and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?
verses.after: Do you know how God directs them and makes his cloud’s lightning shine?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you know how God appoints them and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?

verses.rationale: Retains divine complete-knowledge phrase echoing Elihu’s claim.
verses.before: Do you know the balancing of the clouds, the wonders of one complete in knowledge?
verses.after: Do you know how the clouds hang in balance, the wonders of one complete in knowledge?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you know the balancing of the clouds, the wonders of one complete in knowledge?

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily heat and stillness before question.
verses.before: You whose garments are hot when the earth is still because of the south wind,
verses.after: You whose clothes grow hot when the earth lies still under the south wind,
verses.tsw_comparator: You whose garments are hot when the earth is still because of the south wind,

verses.rationale: Retains ancient solid-sky image without modernizing cosmology.
verses.before: can you, with him, spread out the skies, hard as a cast-metal mirror?
verses.after: can you hammer out the skies with him, hard as a cast-metal mirror?
verses.tsw_comparator: can you, with him, spread out the skies, hard as a cast-metal mirror?

verses.rationale: Keeps darkened understanding and legal preparation.
verses.before: Teach us what we should say to him; we cannot arrange our case because of darkness.
verses.after: Teach us what to say to him; we cannot arrange our case because of darkness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Teach us what we should say to him; we cannot arrange our case because of darkness.

verses.rationale: Preserves dangerous-speech questions and swallowing image.
verses.before: Should it be told him that I would speak? If a man speaks, will he surely be swallowed up?
verses.after: Should he be told that I want to speak? Would anyone ask to be swallowed up?
verses.tsw_comparator: Should it be told him that I would speak? If a man speaks, will he surely be swallowed up?

verses.rationale: Clarifies weather sequence without changing light image.
verses.before: And now people cannot look at the light when it is bright in the skies, after the wind has passed and cleared them.
verses.after: Now no one can look at the light when it shines bright in the skies after the wind has swept them clear.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now people cannot look at the light when it is bright in the skies, after the wind has passed and cleared them.

verses.rationale: Retains north and gold without identifying phenomenon.
verses.before: From the north comes golden splendor; around God is awe-inspiring majesty.
verses.after: From the north comes golden splendor; around God is awesome majesty.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the north comes golden splendor; around God is awe-inspiring majesty.

verses.rationale: Follows oppression reading; answering alternative noted.
verses.before: The Almighty—we cannot find him; he is great in power, and in justice and abundant righteousness he does not afflict.
verses.after: The Almighty—we cannot find him out. He is great in power; in justice and abundant righteousness he does not oppress.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Almighty—we cannot find him; he is great in power, and in justice and abundant righteousness he does not afflict.

verses.rationale: Retains divine disregard for self-claimed wisdom.
verses.before: So people fear him; he does not regard any who are wise in their own heart.”
verses.after: That is why people revere him. He pays no regard to those wise in their own hearts.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore people fear him; he does not regard any who are wise in their own heart.”

verses.rationale: Follows read storm phrase and explicit divine speaker.
verses.before: Then the LORD answered Job from the storm and said:
verses.after: Then the LORD answered Job out of the storm:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD answered Job from the storm and said:

verses.rationale: Keeps challenge focused on speech and understanding.
verses.before: “Who is this who darkens counsel with words without knowledge?
verses.after: “Who is this who darkens counsel with words without knowledge?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Who is this who darkens counsel with words without knowledge?

verses.rationale: Renders girding idiom naturally; retains male addressee.
verses.before: Gird up your waist like a man; I will question you, and you make me know.
verses.after: Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you must answer me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gird up your waist like a man; I will question you, and you make me know.

verses.rationale: Keeps foundation image and pointed invitation.
verses.before: Where were you when I founded the earth? Declare it, if you know understanding.
verses.after: Where were you when I laid the earth’s foundations? Tell me, if you have understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: Where were you when I founded the earth? Declare it, if you know understanding.

verses.rationale: Preserves irony and building measurements.
verses.before: Who set its measurements—surely you know! Or who stretched a measuring line upon it?
verses.after: Who determined its dimensions—surely you know! Who stretched a measuring line across it?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who set its measurements—surely you know! Or who stretched a measuring line upon it?

verses.rationale: Retains architectural earth imagery and continued sentence.
verses.before: Upon what were its bases sunk, or who laid its cornerstone,
verses.after: On what were its bases sunk? Who laid its cornerstone,
verses.tsw_comparator: Upon what were its bases sunk, or who laid its cornerstone,

verses.rationale: Keeps cosmic chorus and heavenly sons.
verses.before: when the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
verses.after: while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
verses.tsw_comparator: when the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

verses.rationale: Preserves sea-birth and containment together.
verses.before: And who shut in the sea with doors when it burst out, coming from the womb,
verses.after: Who shut the sea behind doors when it burst out from the womb,
verses.tsw_comparator: And who shut in the sea with doors when it burst out, coming from the womb,

verses.rationale: Keeps newborn wrapping imagery.
verses.before: when I made cloud its garment and thick darkness its swaddling cloth,
verses.after: when I clothed it with clouds and wrapped it in thick darkness,
verses.tsw_comparator: when I made cloud its garment and thick darkness its swaddling cloth,

verses.rationale: Retains boundary and physical restraint.
verses.before: and I prescribed my boundary for it and set bars and doors,
verses.after: when I marked out its boundary and set its bars and doors,
verses.tsw_comparator: and I prescribed my boundary for it and set bars and doors,

verses.rationale: Makes command natural while preserving wave pride.
verses.before: and said, ‘Thus far you may come, and no farther; here your proud waves will stop’?
verses.after: and said, ‘You may come this far, but no farther; here your proud waves must stop’?
verses.tsw_comparator: and said, ‘Thus far you may come, and no farther; here your proud waves shall stop’?

verses.rationale: Follows read dawn and lifetime contrast.
verses.before: Have you ever in your days commanded the morning or made the dawn know its place,
verses.after: In all your days, have you commanded the morning or shown the dawn its place,
verses.tsw_comparator: Have you ever in your days commanded the morning or made the dawn know its place,

verses.rationale: Retains garment-like earth shaken by dawn.
verses.before: that it might take hold of the edges of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
verses.after: so that it takes hold of the earth’s edges and shakes the wicked out of it?
verses.tsw_comparator: that it might take hold of the edges of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?

verses.rationale: Clarifies implied earth while preserving difficult clothing comparison.
verses.before: It is changed like clay under a seal, and things stand out like a garment.
verses.after: The earth changes like clay under a seal; its features stand out like a garment.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is changed like clay under a seal, and things stand out like a garment.

verses.rationale: Keeps their light paradox and broken oppressive arm.
verses.before: Their light is withheld from the wicked, and the uplifted arm is broken.
verses.after: The wicked are deprived of their light, and the uplifted arm is broken.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their light is withheld from the wicked, and the uplifted arm is broken.

verses.rationale: Preserves inaccessible sea depths.
verses.before: Have you entered the springs of the sea or walked in the searchings of the deep?

verses.before: Will traders bargain over it? Will they divide it among merchants?
verses.after: Will partners bargain over it and divide it among merchants?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will traders bargain over it? Will they divide it among merchants?

verses.rationale: Preserves hunting weapons and body targets.
verses.before: Can you fill its skin with harpoons or its head with fishing spears?
verses.after: Can you fill its hide with harpoons or its head with fishing spears?
verses.tsw_comparator: Can you fill its skin with harpoons or its head with fishing spears?

verses.rationale: Keeps ironic invitation and warning.
verses.before: Put your hand upon it; remember the battle— you will not do it again!
verses.after: Lay your hand on it! Remember the battle—you will not do it again.
verses.tsw_comparator: Put your hand upon it; remember the battle— you will not do it again!

verses.rationale: Clarifies implied capture while preserving sight’s force.
verses.before: Look, one’s hope concerning it is false; is one not cast down even at the sight of it?
verses.after: Any hope of capturing it proves false; is not a person thrown down at the very sight?
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, one’s hope concerning it is false; is one not cast down even at the sight of it?

verses.rationale: Preserves first-person divine turn from creature.
verses.before: No one is so fierce that he dares stir it up. Who then can stand before me?
verses.after: No one is fierce enough to rouse it. Who, then, can stand before me?
verses.tsw_comparator: No one is so fierce that he dares stir it up. Who then is able to stand before me?

verses.rationale: Retains obligation question and universal possession.
verses.before: Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Whatever is under all the heavens is mine.
verses.after: Who has given to me first, so that I must repay? Everything under heaven is mine.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Whatever is under all the heavens is mine.

verses.rationale: Follows written negative rather than read to-it; noted.
verses.before: I will not be silent about its limbs, or the word of its might, or the grace of its form.
verses.after: I will not be silent about its limbs, its mighty strength and graceful form.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will not be silent about its limbs, or the word of its might, or the grace of its form.

verses.rationale: Selects jaw sense of double bridle phrase.
verses.before: Who can uncover the face of its garment? Who can enter its double row of teeth?
verses.after: Who can strip off its outer covering? Who can enter between its double jaws?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who can uncover the face of its garment? Who can enter its double row of teeth?

verses.rationale: Retains facial doors and terrifying teeth.
verses.before: Who can open the doors of its face? Around its teeth is terror.
verses.after: Who can open the doors of its face? Terror surrounds its teeth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who can open the doors of its face? Around its teeth is terror.

verses.rationale: Keeps armor image rather than replacing with scales only.
verses.before: Its back is rows of shields, shut up tightly with a seal.
verses.after: Its pride is its rows of shields, closed tight as a seal.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its back is rows of shields, shut up tightly with a seal.

verses.rationale: Preserves tight joining and excluded breath.
verses.before: One is so near another that no air can come between them.
verses.after: Each fits so closely to the next that no air can pass between them.
verses.tsw_comparator: One is so near another that no air can come between them.

verses.rationale: Retains cumulative description of invulnerability.
verses.before: They cling to one another; they hold together and cannot be separated.
verses.after: They cling to one another, locked together, unable to separate.
verses.tsw_comparator: They cling to one another; they hold together and cannot be separated.

verses.rationale: Keeps fantastic light and recurring dawn image.
verses.before: Its sneezings flash light, and its eyes are like the eyelids of dawn.
verses.after: Its sneezes flash with light; its eyes are like the eyelids of dawn.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its sneezings flash light, and its eyes are like the eyelids of dawn.

verses.rationale: Preserves fire-breathing poetry without naturalizing.
verses.before: From its mouth go burning torches; sparks of fire leap out.
verses.after: Flaming torches pour from its mouth; sparks of fire leap out.
verses.tsw_comparator: From its mouth go burning torches; sparks of fire leap out.

verses.rationale: Selects compressed pot/reed relationship with note.
verses.before: From its nostrils smoke goes out, as from a boiling pot over reeds.
verses.after: Smoke rises from its nostrils like a boiling pot over burning reeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: From its nostrils smoke goes out, as from a boiling pot over reeds.

verses.rationale: Retains fiery breath and mouth.
verses.before: Its breath kindles coals, and flame goes out from its mouth.
verses.after: Its breath sets coals ablaze; a flame comes from its mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its breath kindles coals, and flame goes out from its mouth.

verses.rationale: Keeps personified strength and dancing dread.
verses.before: Strength dwells in its neck, and terror dances before it.
verses.after: Strength dwells in its neck; dismay dances before it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Strength dwells in its neck, and terror dances before it.

verses.rationale: Preserves fused bodily armor image.
verses.before: The folds of its flesh cling together; they are firm upon it and cannot be moved.
verses.after: The folds of its flesh cling together, firmly cast upon it, immovable.
verses.tsw_comparator: The folds of its flesh cling together; they are firm upon it and cannot be moved.

verses.rationale: Keeps specific lower stone comparison.
verses.before: Its heart is hard as stone, hard as the lower millstone.
verses.after: Its heart is cast hard as stone, hard as a lower millstone.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its heart is hard as stone, hard as the lower millstone.

verses.rationale: Selects dismay reading; purifying alternative noted.
verses.before: When it rises, mighty ones are afraid; because of the crashing they lose themselves.
verses.after: When it rises, the mighty are afraid; at its crashing they lose their bearings.
verses.tsw_comparator: When it rises, mighty ones are afraid; because of the crashing they lose themselves.

verses.rationale: Keeps distinct weapons despite rare identifications.
verses.before: The sword that reaches it does not stand, nor spear, dart, or javelin.
verses.after: A sword that reaches it cannot stand, nor spear, dart, or javelin.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sword that reaches it does not stand, nor spear, dart, or javelin.

verses.rationale: Preserves paired material reversals.
verses.before: It regards iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.
verses.after: It counts iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.
verses.tsw_comparator: It regards iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.

verses.rationale: Renders son-of-bow idiom as arrow.
verses.before: An arrow does not make it flee; sling stones become stubble to it.
verses.after: An arrow cannot make it flee; slingstones become chaff to it.
verses.tsw_comparator: An arrow does not make it flee; sling stones become stubble to it.

verses.rationale: Preserves weapon scorn and repeated laughter.
verses.before: Clubs are regarded as stubble, and it laughs at the rattling of the javelin.
verses.after: Clubs are counted as chaff; it laughs at a javelin’s rattling.
verses.tsw_comparator: Clubs are regarded as stubble, and it laughs at the rattling of the javelin.

verses.rationale: Retains pottery and agricultural scar imagery.
verses.before: Its undersides are like sharp potsherds; it spreads a threshing sledge upon the mud.
verses.after: Its underside is sharp as broken pottery; it spreads a threshing sledge across the mud.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its undersides are like sharp potsherds; it spreads a threshing sledge upon the mud.

verses.rationale: Keeps two churning-container comparisons.
verses.before: It makes the deep boil like a pot; it makes the sea like a pot of ointment.
verses.after: It makes the deep boil like a pot, the sea like a vessel of ointment.
verses.tsw_comparator: It makes the deep boil like a pot; it makes the sea like a pot of ointment.

verses.rationale: Retains aged-deep image rather than only describing foam.
verses.before: Behind it, it makes a path shine; one would think the deep had white hair.
verses.after: It leaves a shining path behind it; one would think the deep had turned gray-haired.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behind it, it makes a path shine; one would think the deep had white hair.

verses.rationale: Keeps unrivaled earthly fearlessness.
verses.before: On earth there is nothing like it, a creature made without fear.
verses.after: Nothing on earth is its equal, a creature made without fear.
verses.tsw_comparator: On earth there is nothing like it, a creature made without fear.

verses.rationale: Preserves king and sons-of-pride animal expression.
verses.before: It looks upon everything high; it is king over all the children of pride.”
verses.after: It looks down on all that is lofty; it is king over all the proud beasts.”
verses.tsw_comparator: It looks upon everything high; it is king over all the children of pride.”

verses.rationale: Marks final human reply.
verses.before: Then Job answered the LORD and said:
verses.after: Job answered the LORD:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Job answered the LORD and said:

verses.rationale: Follows read I-know form and unfrustrated purpose.
verses.before: “I know that you can do everything and that no purpose of yours can be withheld.
verses.after: “I know that you can do everything; no purpose of yours can be thwarted.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I know that you can do all things and that no purpose of yours can be withheld.

verses.rationale: Marks recalled divine question and Job’s acknowledgment.
verses.before: ‘Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ So I declared what I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
verses.after: ‘Who is this who conceals counsel without knowledge?’ I have spoken of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, beyond my knowing.
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ Therefore I declared what I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.

verses.rationale: Treats instruction as recalled divine speech; alternative noted.
verses.before: ‘Hear now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you make me know.’
verses.after: ‘Listen now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you must answer me.’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Hear now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you make me know.’

verses.rationale: Keeps hearing-to-seeing change without defining vision.
verses.before: By the hearing of the ear I had heard of you, but now my eye has seen you.
verses.after: I had heard of you with my ears, but now my eyes have seen you.
verses.tsw_comparator: By the hearing of the ear I had heard of you, but now my eye has seen you.

verses.rationale: Supplies speech as implied object; notes repent/comfort alternatives.
verses.before: So I reject and relent concerning dust and ashes.”
verses.after: So I take back what I said and relent in dust and ashes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I reject and relent concerning dust and ashes.”

verses.rationale: Preserves divine distinction from friends; to-me alternative noted.
verses.before: After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My anger burns against you and against your two friends, because you have not spoken concerning me what is right, as my servant Job has.
verses.after: After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, he said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My anger burns against you and your two friends, because you have not spoken rightly about me as my servant Job has.
verses.tsw_comparator: After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My anger burns against you and against your two friends, because you have not spoken concerning me what is right, as my servant Job has.

verses.rationale: Keeps counts, intercession, acceptance, and repeated verdict.
verses.before: So now take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job. Offer a burnt offering for yourselves, and my servant Job will pray for you. For I will accept his face, so that I do not deal with you according to your folly, because you have not spoken concerning me what is right, as my servant Job has.”
verses.after: Now take seven bulls and seven rams, go to my servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you. I will accept him and will not deal with you according to your folly, because you have not spoken rightly about me as my servant Job has.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So now take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job. Offer a burnt offering for yourselves, and my servant Job shall pray for you. For I will accept his face, so that I do not deal with you according to your folly, because you have not spoken concerning me what is right, as my servant Job has.”

verses.rationale: Preserves named three; does not insert Elihu into verdict.
verses.before: Then Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD spoke to them, and the LORD accepted Job’s face.
verses.after: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them, and the LORD accepted Job.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD spoke to them, and the LORD accepted Job’s face.

verses.rationale: Keeps restoration idiom and temporal prayer relationship.
verses.before: The LORD restored the fortunes of Job when he prayed for his friends, and the LORD added to all that Job had, double.
verses.after: The LORD restored Job’s fortunes when he prayed for his friends. The LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD restored the fortunes of Job when he prayed for his friends, and the LORD added to all that Job had, double.

verses.rationale: Retains divine calamity attribution, kin, comfort, and exact gifts.
verses.before: Then all his brothers, all his sisters, and everyone who had known him before came to him and ate bread with him in his house. They showed him sympathy and comforted him concerning all the trouble that the LORD had brought upon him. Each gave him one piece of silver and one gold ring.
verses.after: All his brothers and sisters and everyone who had known him before came and ate with him in his house. They shared his grief and comforted him for all the calamity the LORD had brought upon him. Each gave him one kesitah and one gold ring.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all his brothers, all his sisters, and all who had known him before came to him and ate bread with him in his house. They showed him sympathy and comforted him concerning all the trouble that the LORD had brought upon him. Each gave him one piece of silver and one gold ring.

verses.rationale: Preserves doubled livestock and female donkeys.
verses.before: The LORD blessed the latter days of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and one thousand female donkeys.
verses.after: The LORD blessed Job’s later life more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand pairs of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD blessed the latter days of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and one thousand female donkeys.

verses.rationale: Keeps actual children’s count without doubling it.
verses.before: He also had seven sons and three daughters.
verses.after: He also had seven sons and three daughters.
verses.tsw_comparator: He also had seven sons and three daughters.

verses.rationale: Preserves three names and birth order.
verses.before: He called the name of the first Jemimah, the name of the second Keziah, and the name of the third Keren-Happuch.
verses.after: He named the first daughter Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
verses.tsw_comparator: He called the name of the first Jemimah, the name of the second Keziah, and the name of the third Keren-Happuch.

verses.rationale: Retains text’s beauty claim and daughters’ inheritance.
verses.before: In all the land no women were found as beautiful as Job’s daughters, and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
verses.after: Nowhere in the land were women found as beautiful as Job’s daughters. Their father gave them an inheritance alongside their brothers.
verses.tsw_comparator: In all the land no women were found as beautiful as Job’s daughters, and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.

verses.rationale: Keeps subsequent years and four generations distinct.
verses.before: After this Job lived one hundred forty years and saw his children and his children’s children, four generations.
verses.after: After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: After this Job lived one hundred forty years and saw his children and his children’s children, four generations.

verses.rationale: Retains fullness idiom at narrative close.
verses.before: Then Job died, old and full of days.
verses.after: Then Job died, old and full of days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Job died, old and full of days.
